reasons: Classification is correct: the sole grant clause (p0002) runs only to "Customer", is expressly "revocable" independent of the termination machinery, and names neither Affiliates nor contractors, with the only path to third-party use being Kubient's prior written consent (p0025). That fails the fallback (affiliates on written notice) and touches walk-away territory, so a deviation with a redline is warranted rather than an over-flag of an acceptable fallback.

Redline reaches the playbook position on all three limbs the rule requires: grant extended to "its Affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf", at-will revocation replaced by revocation only on expiry/termination under paragraph 4, and express transferability to a successor via the assignment provisions (consistent with p0072, which the rationale correctly credits).

Consequential deletions of "non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense" are directionally aligned (transferability to successors and affiliate/contractor use cannot coexist with those words) and the 0.473 changed-character ratio is justified by the scope of rewriting the rule demands; the edit stays within the grant sentence and leaves the commercial substance (limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, stated purpose) intact.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook requirement and offers the written-notice fallback, matching required tone and prefix.

Minor gap for the negotiator to watch, not a basis to reject: the third-party-access restriction in p0025 was left unedited and could be read to cut across the new contractor coverage; a conforming carve-out ("except as permitted under the licence in paragraph 2") would make the position airtight.
